item.title: US Police Now Armed With Israeli Spy Vans Simulating Mobile Phone Towers
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Israeli company Cognyte’s Falconet technology lets US law enforcement mount cell-tower simulators in ordinary vehicles, intercepting mobile data from every nearby phone without a warrant. The Texas Department of Public Safety bought four equipped Tahoes for $3.8 million, letting police collect detailed movement and communication records during routine patrols — the same class of device the EFF’s Rayhunter project (below) is built to detect.

item.title: Rayhunter
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: An open-source tool from EFF that detects IMSI catchers (cell-site simulators / Stingrays) — devices that impersonate cell towers to intercept phones. Originally built for the Orbic RC400L mobile hotspot, with community-added support for more hardware since. A concrete, usable way to detect cellular surveillance rather than just read about it.

item.title: Now Google Says It Might Use Your Gmail and Google Photos Data to Target Ads
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Google’s updated privacy policy ties its new ‘Personal Intelligence’ AI features to ad targeting: opting in to let Gemini draw on your Gmail and Google Photos for personalized AI recommendations also opens that same data up for more personalized ads. The AI-features pitch and the ad-targeting expansion are, by design, the same consent.

item.title: Hundreds Support Legal Defense for Engineer Charged with Destroying Flock Surveillance Cameras
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A US Air Force engineer, Jeffrey Sovern, faces criminal charges for allegedly damaging more than a dozen AI-powered Flock license-plate-reader cameras. His legal defense fund has pulled in over $23,000 from 680+ donors who see the act as a response to unaccountable mass-surveillance infrastructure spreading through small towns with little public input.

item.title: How Tech Scammers Conned Four People Out of $673,000 in Three Days
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Four residents of Clallam County, Washington lost over $673,000 in 72 hours to scammers impersonating Microsoft support, crypto platforms, and federal agents — fake security alerts and fabricated criminal investigations pressured victims into gift cards, crypto transfers, and gold bullion purchases. A hard reminder that scam-recognition has to be part of community digital literacy work, not just technical security.

item.title: GoDaddy Warns India's Crackdown on Fake Site Registrars Could Upend Internet Privacy Everywhere
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: An Indian court ordered domain registrars to strip default WHOIS privacy protections and hand over owner information within 72 hours to anyone claiming a ’legitimate interest,’ ostensibly to fight fraud. GoDaddy and other registrars warn the rule exposes ordinary site owners to harassment and stalking while barely slowing actual scammers — and because domain governance is global, a single national court could end anonymous site registration everywhere.

item.title: Geek Feminism Wiki
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A resource for and about women in geek communities, running since May 2008 and covering harassment policies, sexism in tech and SFF fandom, and related ‘issues’ and ‘resources’ categories. The wiki has been in archival mode since the mid-2010s — new edits are restricted and the wiki itself flags that its 2009–2012 content ’likely reflects many undesirable biases, such as racism and ableism,’ kept available as a historical record rather than a maintained resource.

item.title: FSF Shares Update on 'LibrePhone' and New Automated Site Monitoring Tool
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: The Free Software Foundation’s LibrePhone project is reverse-engineering the proprietary firmware blobs inside smartphones — lead developer Rob Savoye has already extracted and analyzed radio firmware from over 200 LineageOS-supported devices. It’s a reminder that even ‘open’ phones still run closed, unauditable code on the WiFi, Bluetooth, and cellular radios — exactly the layer where most interception and tracking happens.

item.title: Edward Snowden Reveals How They Spy on You
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A video built around Edward Snowden’s account of NSA mass-surveillance programs — the scope of bulk data and metadata collection he exposed in 2013. Published by the channel Thinkable rather than an outlet directly affiliated with Snowden, so treat it as a secondary explainer/compilation rather than primary reporting.

item.title: Become the Thousand Servers
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A field guide arguing that infrastructure resilience comes from spreading technical knowledge across a group, not from concentrating it in one skilled person or one well-maintained server. It walks through mapping dependencies, managing backups, and migrating services, aiming to make collective projects survive the disappearance of any single person or provider: ‘one person learning something, teaching someone else, and watching that knowledge move outward.’

item.title: Automatic Transmission: A Privacy Study of Connected Vehicles
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Billed as the first large-scale measurement study of the connected-vehicle ecosystem, this Northeastern/Consumer Reports research examined 21 vehicles and 30 companion apps and found most cars contact advertising and tracking domains by default — with companion apps substantially expanding what’s collected beyond what manufacturers disclose. The gap between stated privacy policy and actual data flows is the headline finding.

item.title: Are Wars Blurring Lines Between Corporate and National Security?
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Modern conflict increasingly targets privately-owned infrastructure — subsea cables, power stations, ports, data centers — collapsing the line between corporate assets and national security. NATO is now funding protection of private infrastructure as a defense expenditure, raising the question of who actually controls, and who’s liable for, the physical backbone the internet and power grid run on.

item.title: Abya Yala Network: Enabling Community-Owned Internet Infrastructure Across the Americas
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: The Abya Yala Network helps Indigenous peoples, environmental defenders, and grassroots groups across the Americas build and run their own communication infrastructure — training communities to ‘be their own (and each other’s) system administrators’ with open-source tools instead of depending on corporate platforms. A concrete, funded example of the community-owned-infrastructure model this site keeps pointing toward.

item.title: A Fundamental Flaw Leaves LLMs Strikingly Vulnerable To Attack
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Researchers presented findings at ICML showing that LLMs have a structural weakness in how they distinguish instructions from different sources — attackers can exploit that confusion to bypass safety guardrails. The researchers argue the flaw may not be patchable through better training alone, since it’s rooted in how the models process ‘roles’ at all, not a fixable bug in one system.

item.title: What is a Feminist Server?
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: What would it mean to build digital infrastructure that embodies feminist values — not just in content policy but in governance, ownership, and who the infrastructure serves? Examines feminist server collectives as an alternative model to corporate platforms and explores what accountable, community-governed technology looks like in practice.

item.title: The Road to Techno-Colonialism
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Traces how tech corporations replicate the patterns of colonial extraction — entering new markets, crowding out local alternatives, creating dependency, and extracting value back to distant centers — while framing this as development and connectivity. Useful grounding for understanding why digital infrastructure is never politically neutral.

item.title: The New Luddites
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: An examination of the growing neo-Luddite movement — people choosing to reject or limit their engagement with surveillance capitalism’s tools, not out of technophobia but out of political clarity about what those tools do. Situates this in the history of the original Luddites as a labor and rights movement, not an anti-technology one.

item.title: Surveillance Valley: The Secret Military History of the Internet
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Levine’s investigation into the ARPANET’s origins and the unbroken line between the internet’s military-surveillance roots and today’s tech industry. Essential background for anyone serious about understanding what the network actually is.

item.title: Sentinels Network
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A platform built for and by Indigenous communities to monitor, manage, and protect their lands and waters using community-controlled data infrastructure. A concrete example of what Indigenous data sovereignty looks like in practice — ecological monitoring on Indigenous terms, governed by Indigenous protocols.

item.title: Never Again Tech — Tech Worker Pledge
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A public pledge by technology workers to refuse to build databases of people by race, religion, or national origin; refuse to build tools for mass surveillance; and resist government use of their skills to target people for discriminatory programs. Thousands of signatories from companies including Google, Microsoft, and Amazon.

item.title: Keeping Indigenous Science Knowledge out of a Colonial Mold
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: How researchers and Indigenous communities are working to document and protect traditional ecological knowledge without forcing it into Western scientific frameworks that strip it of relational context. Addresses the real tension between making TEK legible to outside institutions and maintaining community control over how it moves.

item.title: Indigenous Mapping Collective
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Community-led mapping initiatives centering Indigenous peoples’ relationships to land. A model for what it looks like when technically skilled people work in genuine solidarity — transferring capacity rather than extracting data.

item.title: Indigenous Knowledge, Western Science, and the US Colonial Project
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: How Western scientific institutions have historically appropriated, dismissed, and suppressed Indigenous knowledge systems while simultaneously depending on Indigenous land and labor. Examines the colonial structure of American science and what genuine knowledge sovereignty would require.

item.title: IndieWeb — Own Your Data
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A community and movement built around the principle that people should own their own data and content — publishing on their own domains, using open standards to connect and communicate, rather than depending on corporate platforms that can disappear or change the rules without notice. Practical guides, standards, and community resources.

item.title: Have I Been Flocked?
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Search whether your license plate has been captured in Flock Safety’s automated license plate reader (ALPR) database — over 208 million documented searches. Publishes public records on how law enforcement agencies use Flock surveillance, including searches tied to First Amendment activities and immigration enforcement.

item.title: EFF: Age Verification
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: The EFF’s ongoing coverage and analysis of age verification legislation — tracking bills across states and Congress, explaining the surveillance and free speech implications, and documenting legal challenges. A reliable reference for understanding the landscape of these laws and the harms they cause.

item.title: DataBack: Recognize and Reclaim Indigenous Data Sovereignty
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: An introduction to the #DataBack movement — what it means for Indigenous communities to reclaim authority over data about their lands, cultures, and peoples. Situates data sovereignty within the broader LandBack and CashBack frameworks and explains why control of data is inseparable from political and cultural self-determination.

item.title: Claude Code Prompt Steganography
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A developer inspecting Claude Code for privacy reasons found that it steganographically embeds hidden markers in its system prompts — identifiers derived from your API base URL and timezone, invisible to users but present in every request. When a coding agent has filesystem, shell, and git access to your work, the binary shipping it should be transparent about what it’s sending.

item.title: CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: The CARE Principles — Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics — are a governance framework developed by Indigenous data scholars to center Indigenous peoples in all decisions about their data. A complement and counterweight to the FAIR data principles that dominate academic and government data practice.

item.title: AI: Real Problems Index
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A running index of documented real-world harms from AI systems — not speculation about future risks, but concrete cases of bias, discrimination, misinformation, environmental damage, labor exploitation, and rights violations happening now. A useful counter to the hype cycle.

item.title: A Website to End All Websites
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A personal essay/manifesto arguing that the internet has been industrialized and monopolized by corporate platforms that exploit users rather than serve them — and that the answer is building hand-coded personal websites using open protocols like RSS and ActivityPub. Draws on Ivan Illich’s concept of ‘convivial tools’ that enhance human creativity rather than capture it.

item.title: Age Verification Is Just a Precursor to Attribution of Speech
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: Age verification laws ostensibly protect children but actually build identity attribution infrastructure — systems that automatically link digital accounts to real identities. Once in place, that infrastructure will be turned toward political speech and dissent. The child safety framing is the door; surveillance is what walks through it.

item.title: How Did Free Software Build a Social Movement?
item.author: contact@klamathtech.diy (ҜŁΔΜΔŦĦ Ŧ€ĆĦ ĆØŁŁ€ĆŦƗV€)
item.description: A history of how the free and open-source software movement grew from technical practice into political organizing — the values, the licenses, the communities, and the fights over what ‘free’ actually means. Useful context for understanding why software freedom and community autonomy are connected questions.
